mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which compresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO contraction below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and inflation, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL are above their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between monthly changes in real personal income (proxied by GDPC1) and monthly changes in S&P 500 returns over the past 12 months indicates that continued income growth will sustain consumer spending and drive further equity gains over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between GDPC1 growth and S&P 500 returns breaks down (p > 0.10) or S&P 500 does not produce positive 60-day returns when GDPC1 grows above trend.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE in the same month signals a paradoxical labor market shock (e.g., mass hiring at low wage growth), which can destabilize expectations and trigger negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both PAYEMS and UNRATE increase in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average, coupled with a concurrent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), signals weakening housing and consumption demand, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-month MA AND GDPC1 < 12-month MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both HOUST and GDPC1 fall below their 12-month moving averages in the same month.
